The Build

Sustainabox is a custom container home built from one 20-foot and two 40-foot high-cube (HC) one-trip shipping containers. Set on pier foundations and connected by a deck to create a courtyard, the layout balances comfort, function, and adaptability.

We're using a combination of detailed SketchUp models, hand-drawn diagrams, and site surveys to guide the build and coordinate with trades.

C1

Container 1

40-foot HC one-trip

Main living space with kitchen, living room, and 1/2 bathroom. Sits at the rear of the build site, parallel to the road.

C2

Container 2

40-foot HC one-trip

Positioned to the right side and connected with C1 at the rear left corner. Houses two bedrooms, a full bathroom, and a utility space with washer/dryer.

C3

Container 3

20-foot HC one-trip

Parallel to C2 on the left side. A flex space — office, guest room, and storage. Power and AC, no plumbing. Sits separately from the main layout.

Drawings

These drawings include a mix of exports from our SketchUp 3D model and hand-drawn details. We update this section as the design evolves and as trades provide input.

Survey

The survey was provided during the property purchase and shows the full lot, including the small piece of land that was added years ago and officially merged into the parcel. It captures early topographic details and key landmarks, such as the original wood shed, which has since been removed. The entire foundation and container placement were aligned around this feature.

Elevation

The elevation views were generated using geospatial mapping tools within SketchUp, pulling real-world terrain data and surrounding structures into the model. This tool has been incredibly useful for visualizing how the containers sit on the land.

Foundation

The Sustainabox foundation is built using reinforced concrete piers designed to support the weight and structural demands of C1 and C2. C3 will have a temporary foundation.

Interior

C1 and C2 will be framed with metal studs, insulated using closed-cell spray foam, and finished with drywall. Container 3 will take a simpler approach with plywood walls and no plumbing.

Systems

Electrical

The electrical plans outline key circuits for each container, including dedicated runs for major appliances, lighting, switches, outlets, and utility connections. C3 will have a simplified 120V layout pending final AC requirements.

Plumbing

The plumbing layout covers fixture locations, supply and drain lines, and utility connections. C1 includes the kitchen, half bathroom, and tie-ins for hot water and filtration. C2 includes the main bathroom and laundry/utility connections.
